title: EncodePartOptions<'a> has a lifetime parameter in the public API
description: EncodePartOptions in yencoding/src/lib.rs carries a lifetime parameter `<'a>` because it holds a `filename: Option<&'a str>`. This lifetime leaks into the public API: callers must name the lifetime in their own code, and the struct cannot be stored in a struct without the struct also carrying a lifetime. What goes wrong: if the crate later wants to switch filename to an owned String (e.g. to allow construction from computed names), that is a breaking change — the lifetime disappears from the signature. Using `filename: Option<String>` with a `with_filename(&str)` builder method would be lifetime-free and equally efficient at the call site. File: yencoding/src/lib.rs.
close_reason: EncodePartOptions<'a> lifetime is intentional — it borrows filename from the caller, avoiding an allocation. Changing to owned String would be an API regression for the common case. Opinion.
